data.title: You have been Hacked!
data.statement:
Hackers carry out Advanced Persistent Threat cyber attacks against a number of companies. Each company has a firewall with a protection level [[p]].

<<Cyber attack stages>>

Hackers execute 3 types of attack in the following order:

1 - Port scanning ({{ps}})
2 - Brute force ({{bf}})
3 - Malware installation ({{mi}})

There may be multiple attack attempts against the same company in a single stage. The <<sum>> of their strengths is used to evaluate the stage. If a stage is successful, the attack proceeds to the next stage; otherwise, the attack is blocked and later stages are not evaluated.

Once the next stage begins, no further attempts of the previous stage occur.

If any stage is blocked, the company's status is {{Blocked}}. If all three stages are successful, its status is {{Hacked}}.

<<Firewall rules>>

The firewall behaves according to its protection level as follows. Each number in columns 2 to 4 is the <<exclusive>> upper bound on the total attack strength that the firewall can block.

Firewall       Port         Brute        Malware
protection     scanning     force        installation
level ([[p]])     ({{ps}})         ({{bf}})         ({{mi}})
[[p]] ≥ 7          10000        ∞            ∞
5 ≤ [[p]] ≤ 6      0            5000         3000
[[p]] < 5          0            500          1000

For example:
• {{10000}} means that the attack is blocked if the total strength is strictly less than 10000.
• {{0}} means that the attack is always successful (not blocked).
• {{∞}} means that the attack is always blocked.

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

Hackers carry out Advanced Persistent Threat cyber attacks against a number of companies. Each company has a firewall with a protection level p.

Cyber attack stages

Hackers execute 3 types of attack in the following order:

1 - Port scanning (ps)
2 - Brute force (bf)
3 - Malware installation (mi)

There may be multiple attack attempts against the same company in a single stage. The sum of their strengths is used to evaluate the stage. If a stage is successful, the attack proceeds to the next stage; otherwise, the attack is blocked and later stages are not evaluated.

Once the next stage begins, no further attempts of the previous stage occur.

If any stage is blocked, the company's status is Blocked. If all three stages are successful, its status is Hacked.

Firewall rules

The firewall behaves according to its protection level as follows. Each number in columns 2 to 4 is the exclusive upper bound on the total attack strength that the firewall can block.

Firewall Port Brute Malware
protection scanning force installation
level (p) (ps) (bf) (mi)
p ≥ 7 10000 ∞ ∞
5 ≤ p ≤ 6 0 5000 3000
p < 5 0 500 1000

For example:
• 10000 means that the attack is blocked if the total strength is strictly less than 10000.
• 0 means that the attack is always successful (not blocked).
• ∞ means that the attack is always blocked.
Input
Line 1: An integer n, the number of companies.
Next n Lines: A string in the format of name:p where name (string) is the company's name and p (integer) is its firewall protection level. (These lines collectively form the company list.)
Line + 2 n: An integer a, the number of cyber attack attempts.
Next a Lines: A string in the format of name:type:s where name is the attacked company's name, type is the attack stage (ps, bf, or mi), and s is the attack strength.
Output
n Lines: name:status
where name is the company's name, and status is the status of the cyber attack on the company (Hacked or Blocked).
The output order is the same as the order of companies in the company list.
Constraints
1 ≤ n ≤ 10
1 ≤ length of name ≤ 30
1 ≤ p ≤ 10
1 ≤ a ≤ 100
1 ≤ s ≤ 20000
name never contains :.
All names in the company list are unique.
There is always at least one attack of each type against every company, and the attacks for each company are always in the correct order.
Example
Input
1

4
